text:
maria: Heads-up — last night's cron janitor + bench-suite-v2 run failed and kicked off a cascade of CI reds. I pulled the logs, looks like a mix of OOM + a permission error during checkpoint cleanup. Can someone triage? cc @aj @kevin :eyes:

aj: on it. I'm seeing shard=7 spike GPU mem then the cleanup fails. Pasting the tail: 
```
W tensorflow: OutOfMemoryError: failed to allocate 3.2G
ERROR: cleanup: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/mnt/checkpoints/tmp-185123'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/cron/janitor.py\", line 214, in cleanup_checkpoints
    os.remove(path)
PermissionError: [Errno 13] 
```

kevin: hmm looks like two issues. OOM on bench-worker (batch size too large for new model variant), and janitor ran as a different uid so couldn't remove tmp dir. Ops probably changed the service account last deploy.

sam: quick triage plan: 1) rerun failing shard with smaller batch 2) add --safe-cleanup flag so janitor uses sudo-like flow 3) bisect to see which model change increased memory.

ops-jenna: I can revert the service-account tweak for janitor in staging; will need a quick PR. For prod I'm hesitant without a canary.

maria: can we at least rerun the nightly bench shard to unflake CI? if it passes we can leave prod changes for tomorrow.

ci-bot: nightly-bench-v2 (shard=7) failed — exit code 137 (OOM) — https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/8484843

infra-bot: queued rerun for nightly-bench-v2 shard=7 with env BATCH_SIZE=8 — run id 8484860 — triggered by aj

aj: kicked rerun with smaller batch and --collect-kv-stats. also added `--tmp-dir /scratch/aj` to avoid janitor race.

kevin: thanks. can you also capture dmesg / nvml logs if it hits OOM again? saves time for bisect.

aj: will attach logs if it fails. current rerun: https://ci.internal/redwood/runs/8484860

infra-bot: rerun completed: PASS ✅ — nightly-bench-v2 shard=7 — run id 8484860 — duration 12m

aj: pass confirmed. looks like batch-size was the culprit for this shard. still curious about permission denied — ops-jenna did you see that in staging?

ops-jenna: I investigated the SA change — it affected only the janitor in the staging cluster (wrong namespace binding). I fixed the binding in staging and opened PR #1227 to fix prod binding.

maria: great — can you link the PR and create INF ticket to ensure we don't accidentally change SA bindings next deploy?

ops-jenna: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1227 — created INF-459: "janitor service-account binding causes checkpoint cleanup perm errors" and assigned to infra oncall.

sam: leaving a note to add a flaky test entry for shard=7 in our bench health dashboard + add a safety limit to batch-size in runner config.

maria: thanks all. closing this thread — reopen if rerun flakes or janitor still reports permission errors. :white_check_mark:
